question: Our body works within the pH range of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**7 to 7.8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The normal pH range of the human body is tightly regulated between **7.35 and 7.45**.
 
• This pH range is considered slightly alkaline and is essential for the proper functioning of biochemical processes.
 
• A pH below 7.35 indicates a condition called **acidosis**, while a pH above 7.45 indicates **alkalosis**.
 
• Maintaining this pH range is crucial for the body's enzyme activity and metabolic processes.
 
• The kidneys and lungs play a significant role in regulating the body’s pH balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acidosis**

 
 
• Acidosis is a condition where the body’s pH falls below 7.35.
 
• It can result from increased acid production, decreased acid excretion, or a loss of bicarbonate.
 
• Symptoms may include fatigue, confusion, and shortness of breath.
 
 
 
• **Alkalosis**
 
 
• Alkalosis occurs when the body’s pH rises above 7.45.
 
• It can be caused by a loss of acid or an excess of bicarbonate.
 
• Symptoms may include muscle twitching, hand tremor, and light-headedness.
 
 
 
• **Buffer Systems**
 
 
• Buffer systems in the body, such as the bicarbonate buffer system, help maintain pH balance.
 
• These systems neutralize excess acids or bases to prevent drastic changes in pH.
 
 
 
• **Role of Kidneys and Lungs**
 
 
• The kidneys regulate pH by excreting hydrogen ions and reabsorbing bicarbonate from urine.
 
• The lungs regulate pH by controlling the levels of carbon dioxide through breathing.
